extracted.intended_audience: TeX implementers, advanced TeX users, font designers, and professional typesetters
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed low-level rules and parameter conventions for converting TeX math lists into boxes (math typesetting) and for hyphenation using Liang's algorithm and TeX's exception/pattern mechanisms. Includes per-item processing rules (Rules 1–22), sub/superscript positioning, fraction/radical/accent construction, inter-element spacing, penalty insertion, and hyphenation pattern/exception syntax and behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1: leave rule/discretionary/penalty/whatsit/boundary items unchanged
rubrics_metrics.description: If the current item is a rule or discretionary or penalty or 'whatsit' or boundary item, simply leave it unchanged and move to the next item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items are not transformed during the first pass of math-list translation; they remain as-is for later processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 2: translate glue and kern (mu→absolute conversion and \nonscript handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the current item is glue or a kern, translate it: convert mu units from \mskip or \mkern to absolute units by multiplying each finite dimension appropriately; if glue is from \nonscript, check the immediately following item and possibly remove it if certain conditions hold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special-case \nonscript glue: if immediately following item is glue or kern and condition C ≤ S holds, remove the following item. Convert mu glue to absolute units as specified so spacing is correct in non-math-unit dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 3: style-change items
rubrics_metrics.description: If the current item is a style change, set C to the specified style, delete the style-change item, and continue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style-change items affect the 'current style' used for subsequent translations; they are removed during the pass after updating C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 4: four-way choice items (style-dependent lists)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the item is a four-way choice (contains four math lists for the four main styles), replace it by the math list corresponding to the current style C and continue processing from the first unprocessed item of that list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This implements size/style substitutions (e.g., display/text/script/script-script) by selecting the appropriate sublist early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5: Bin atom initial-context conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: If the current item is a Bin atom and it is the first atom in the list or the most recent previous atom was Bin/Op/Rel/Open/Punct, change the current Bin to Ord (then continue with Rule 14); otherwise proceed to Rule 17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enforces context-sensitive class changing of '+'-like tokens when they appear at starts or after certain atom types so spacing and behavior match mathematical conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 6: fix previous Bin when following atom is Rel/Close/Punct
rubrics_metrics.description: If the current item is a Rel or Close or Punct atom and the most recent previous atom was Bin, change that previous Bin to Ord, then continue with Rule 17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures a preceding Bin is not left in a binary role when syntax makes it an ordinary symbol (affects spacing and classification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 7: Open or Inner atom short-circuit
rubrics_metrics.description: If the current item is an Open or Inner atom, go directly to Rule 17 (i.e., no special earlier handling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open/Inner atoms are handled in the later stages where nucleus translation and sub/superscript attachment occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 8: \vcenter atoms converted to Ord and axis-based adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: If the current item is a vcenter atom, let its nucleus be a vbox of height+depth v; change its height to ½v + a and depth to ½v − a (where a is axis height a22), change atom type to Ord, and continue with Rule 17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centers vcenter material around TeX's math axis by redistributing height/depth and treating it as an ordinary atom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 9: Over atoms (\overline) construct vbox with rule above
rubrics_metrics.description: For an Over atom, set box x to the nucleus in style C'; replace the nucleus by a vbox consisting of kern e, hrule of height e, kern 3e, and box x (top to bottom), where e is the default rule thickness; continue with Rule 16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an overline with specified clearances (3e) and assumes e units of extra white space above the rule. Uses default_rule_thickness parameter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 10: Under atoms (\underline) construct vtop with rule below
rubrics_metrics.description: For an Under atom, set box x to nucleus in style C, replace nucleus by a vtop made from box x, kern 3e, and hrule of height e (e = default rule thickness), add e to the depth of the box, and continue with Rule 16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places a rule under the nucleus with 3e clearance and assumes e units of extra white space below the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 11: Radical atoms (\radical / \sqrt) construction rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For a Radical atom, compute e (default rule thickness), compute minimum clearance µ (called ϕ or similar) between the radical's rule and the nucleus, select a variable delimiter of sufficient height+depth, set rule thickness from delimiter font (h(y)), adjust µ if delimiter depth exceeds nucleus size, and construct a vbox consisting of kern, hrule, and the nucleus box; replace nucleus by a raised variable delimiter box and the new vbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The font's delimiter metrics determine the rule thickness and delimiter size; increases in delimiter depth above the nucleus increase clearance. Follow the detailed arithmetic in the text to ensure correct vertical spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 12: Math accents (\mathaccent) positioning and construction
rubrics_metrics.description: If the accent character exists in the current size, set box x to the nucleus in style C', compute nucleus width n and possible italic correction 𝛿 (skew), choose accent successor if width ≤ n, set J = min(h(x), x-height_of_accent_font), if nucleus is single character, package nucleus with its sub/superscripts in style C and empty those fields, put accent into a box including italic correction, build vbox z combining accent and nucleus with computed kerns and shifts, adjust heights/depths as needed, replace nucleus by box z and continue with Rule 16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses font parameter 5 (x-height) and the font's skewchar; handles single-character nuclei specially so accent placement accounts for superscripts/subscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 13: Operators (Op atoms) and limit determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark Op atoms as having limits if marked \limits or (\displaylimits and current style C > T). If nucleus is a symbol, possibly move to a successor glyph for larger display sizes, put symbol in a new box shifted vertically to center on the axis, and set italic correction J included in width if limits are set or there is no subscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large operators (e.g., Σ, ∫) change to larger glyphs in display styles; whether limits are set affects whether the italic correction contributes to width and later placement of limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 13a: Typesetting limits for Op atoms
rubrics_metrics.description: If limits are to be typeset, set boxes for the superscript field (style C¹), nucleus (style C), and subscript (style C+), rebox all to width = max(widths), attach superscript above nucleus separated by kern = max(e₉, e₁₁ - d(x)) with horizontal shifts/extra kerns as specified, attach subscript below similarly, and make the resulting vbox the nucleus of the Op atom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the big-Op-spacing parameters and default rule thickness e to compute vertical separations and horizontal shifts for proper limit placement. The text gives exact formulas for kerns and horizontal shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 14: Ord atoms—ligatures and implicit kerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Ord atoms usually go to Rule 17, unless nucleus is a symbol, both sub/superscripts empty, next item is one of specific atom types and shares the same font family—then mark current symbol as a text symbol; if font info shows a ligature for the pair, insert ligature character(s); if font shows a kern between them, insert a kern item accordingly; after ligature/kern processing go to Rule 17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handles font ligatures and inter-character kerns within mathematical symbols; uses fontdimen info to decide italic corrections and ligature behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 15: Generalized fractions (\over, \atop, \above and delimiters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle generalized fractions by selecting bar thickness e depending on generator (\over → e = default_rule_thickness, \atop → e = 0, \above → specified e), record left/right delimiters (if present), and proceed to construct numerator/denominator boxes and combine them with appropriate vertical shifts and optional rule bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subrules 15a–15e give the exact style choices for numerator/denominator, tentative vertical shifts n and v, minimum clearances ϕ, adjustments when e = 0 (\atop) or e ≠ 0 (\over), and final enclosure by delimiters of sufficient size centered on the axis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 15a: Put numerator/denominator into boxes with appropriate styles
rubrics_metrics.description: Put numerator into box x using style T (or T' if C is D or D'); put denominator into box z using style T' if C > T otherwise C+; rebox the smaller to the larger width so numerator and denominator have same width.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures numerator and denominator align vertically/centrally by equalizing widths before building fraction vbox.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 15b: Tentative vertical shifts n and v for fractions
rubrics_metrics.description: Set tentative upward shift n and downward shift v according to display vs text style (use parameters a(−1), a9, a10, a12 etc.) so numerator is shifted up by n and denominator down by v unless boxes are unusually large.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values depend on whether formula is display or text style and on the particular fraction-generation command used; see the parameter table for exact mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 15c: Combine numerator/denominator for \atop (e = 0)
rubrics_metrics.description: When e = 0, compute minimum clearance ϕ (7e(−1) or 3e(−1) depending on style), get actual clearance θ = (n − depth(x)) − (height(z) − v); if θ < ϕ increase n and v by ½(ϕ − θ) each, then construct vbox of height h(x) + n and depth d(z) + v with appropriate kern between boxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guarantees minimum spacing between numerator and denominator when no rule bar is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 15d: Combine numerator/denominator for \over (e ≠ 0) with bar line
rubrics_metrics.description: When e ≠ 0, set ϕ (3e(−1) or 0 depending on style) as minimum clearance between numerator/denominator and bar, place bar center at axis height a, adjust n and v so clearances meet ϕ, then make vbox ordering box x, kern, hrule (height e), kern, box z with kerns chosen so hrule bottom is at a − ½e above baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate placement of the fraction bar around the math axis is critical; follow axis-height and default_rule_thickness parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 15e: Enclose fraction vbox by delimiters and replace by Inner atom
rubrics_metrics.description: Enclose the constructed vbox by delimiters whose height+depth is at least a specified parameter (azo or az1 depending on style), shift delimiters to be vertically centered on the axis, and replace the generalized fraction by an Inner atom whose nucleus is left-delimiter, vbox, right-delimiter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use delimiter sizing rules (delimiterfactor, delimitershortfall) and center with respect to axis; choose variable delimiters if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 16: Convert current item to Ord and continue to sub/sup handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Change the current item to an Ord atom and continue with Rule 17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardizes item type so subsequent nucleus translation and attachment logic applies uniformly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 17: Nucleus translation to box and italic correction handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If the nucleus is a math list, replace it by a box obtained by typesetting that list in the current style; otherwise (common case) convert symbol to character box for specified family and style, set italic correction J (fontdimen 2) if not marked as text symbol and if fontdimen 2 ≠ 0, and if J nonzero and subscript empty insert a kern of width J after the character box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is where character glyph conversion and italic-correction insertion occur; fontdimen parameters are consulted to decide corrections and kern insertions prior to attaching subscripts/superscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 18: Attaching subscripts and superscripts (general scheme)
rubrics_metrics.description: If neither subscript nor superscript present move on; otherwise follow subrules 18a–18f to compute tentative n and v, create boxes for scripts in appropriate styles, add \scriptspace to their widths, enforce minimum vertical offsets (including limits related to x-height fractions), and if both are present ensure clearance between them at least 4e with adjustments as needed; finally combine nucleus and scripts into vbox with horizontal displacements and append.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed formulas (18a–18f) compute baseline shifts, ensure scripts don't intrude beyond font-specific fractions of x-height, and ensure minimum spacing between joint sub/superscript combinations; default_rule_thickness e and font-based parameters (a1, a9, a10, a12, etc.) are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 19: Boundary item replacement by delimiters sized to formula extent
rubrics_metrics.description: If math list begins and ends with boundary items, compute maximum height h and depth d of boxes in translation, let a be axis height a22 and J = max(h − a, d + a), replace boundary items by delimiters whose height+depth ≥ max(J/500 * f, 2J − l) where f = \delimiterfactor and l = \delimitershortfall, shift delimiters to be vertically centered with respect to axis, and change left/right boundaries to Open/Close atoms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boundary delimiters are sized to cover the full vertical extent of the formula; precise formulas use delimiterfactor and delimitershortfall to pick delimiter size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 20: Second pass—replace atoms by boxes and insert inter-element spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: After Rules 1–19 convert the math list into atoms of the remaining types (Ord, Op, Bin, Rel, Open, Close, Punct, Inner). Make a second pass replacing all atoms by their translated boxes and kerns and insert inter-element spacing before each atom except the first, based on the atom type pair and parameters \thinmuskip, \medmuskip, and \thickmuskip (mu converted to absolute units as in Rule 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter-element spacing depends on the pair of adjacent atom classes and is defined in Chapter 18; mu units conversion must be performed consistently with earlier rules and style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 21: Insert penalties after Bin and Rel atoms in paragraph math lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties are placed after the translation of each atom of type Bin or Rel if the math list was part of a paragraph. The penalty after a Bin is \binoppenalty and after a Rel is \relpenalty, except do not insert if it's the final item in entire list, the penalty value ≥ 100001, next item already a penalty, or after a Rel immediately followed by another Rel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalties influence line-breaking behavior in paragraph math; observe the exceptions to avoid spurious penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 22: Enclose inline math and record \mathsurround; displayed formulas handled later
rubrics_metrics.description: After conversion to horizontal list, if the result is being inserted into a larger horizontal list (horizontal or restricted horizontal mode) enclose it by 'math-on' and 'math-off' items that each record the current value of \mathsurround; if the list is a displayed formula process further as explained in Chapter 19.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: \mathsurround records extra horizontal space around inline math; displayed math follows additional layout steps handled elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font and non-font parameters affecting math typesetting (summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of fontdimen parameters (various fontdimen indices: e.g., space=fontdimen2, x-height=fontdimen5, italic correction, big-Op-spacing parameters, sup/sub parameters, delim parameters) and non-font parameters (\delimitershortfall, \nulldelimiterspace, \mathsurround, \scriptspace, \delimiterfactor, \binoppenalty, \relpenalty, \thinmuskip, \medmuskip, \thickmuskip) influence the behavior of Rules 1–22.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully set these parameters for new mathematical fonts or macros to ensure correct accent placement, operator sizing, fraction clearances, delimiter sizing, inter-element spacing, penalties, and script positioning. The appendix provides mappings from external names (e.g., :sup2) to fontdimen indices and rule references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation principle 1: try exception dictionary first
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX hyphenates a word by first looking for it in an 'exception dictionary' that specifies hyphen positions for words needing special treatment; if not found, patterns are used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception entries must match exactly (after lowercase conversion via \lccode); exception dictionary overrides pattern results and is global in scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation principle 2: Liang's pattern algorithm (patterns → inter-letter values → odd=hyphen)
rubrics_metrics.description: Liang's algorithm extends a word with markers at ends, considers all subwords of varying lengths, matches subwords against a pattern dictionary whose patterns carry inter-letter integer values, computes the maximum value at each potential hyphenation position, and accepts a hyphen at positions where the maximal value is odd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patterns encode desirability (digits 0–9) for hyphenation points; matching and maximization are efficient and language-adaptable. Example: 'hyphenation' yields markers and patterns producing odd values at 'hy-phen-ation'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern syntax and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: A (pattern) consists of one or more occurrences of (value)(letter) followed by (value), where (value) is a digit 0–9 or empty (meaning zero), and (letter) is a character token category 11 or 12 whose \lccode is nonzero; '.' is treated as a letter of code 0 in patterns to represent word edges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To include a digit as a letter in a pattern, precede it by a nonempty value; patterns are strict in character types and are intended to be precompiled by experts (plain TeX loads a large static set).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern application detail: maximal inter-letter value selection
rubrics_metrics.description: For each inter-letter position in the extended word, TeX gathers all pattern-supplied values that touch that position and takes the maximum; hyphenation is allowed where this maximum is odd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example calculations are shown in text (e.g., how patterns produce 'hy-phen-ation' by maximizing values from different matched patterns).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern coverage and derivation (Liang's method and data sources)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patterns can be derived by analyzing a hyphenated dictionary (Liang used a special Webster's Pocket Dictionary and a hyphenation dictionary from a publisher), weighting common words more heavily; plain TeX's English patterns (4,447 patterns) find ~89.3% of hyphens in Liang's dictionary and guarantee complete hyphenation for the ~700 most common English words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pattern sets are language-specific; deriving good patterns requires curated corpora and may include adding exceptional words after testing against larger dictionaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception dictionary format and rules for \hyphenation{...}
rubrics_metrics.description: The \hyphenation{words} command takes words (one or more) separated by spaces; each word item must consist wholly of letters and hyphens (a 'hyphen' is token -, category code 12), letters are characters with category codes 11 or 12 or control-sequences via \chardef/\char whose character has nonzero \lccode; TeX uses \lccode to convert letters to lowercase for matching; exception entries affect hyphenation only on exact lowercase match and are global.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions never insert hyphens after the very first letter or before the last or second-last letter unless you explicitly include discretionary hyphens in the entry. If the same word is specified more than once, the most recent entry wins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commands for debugging/inspecting hyphenation: \showhyphens
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \showhyphens{<text>} to display terminal/log output of hyphenation points TeX would find for the text; the macro constructs an intentionally underfull hbox so hyphens are shown in compact form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ignore the spurious 'Underfull \hbox (badness 10000)' warning that arises because the display technique purposely makes an underfull box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern loading: static patterns vs dynamic exception dictionary
rubrics_metrics.description: The exception dictionary is dynamic (can be modified at run-time via \hyphenation) but the pattern dictionary is static in production TeX: to change the pattern set you must create a new format using INITEX and a \patterns{...} list (INITEX precompresses patterns into a format file for fast loading by production TeX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pattern compression requires extra INITEX-time memory; production versions load precompiled pattern tables rapidly and cannot accept \patterns at runtime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word recognition for hyphenation (what counts as a word)
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX recognizes words for hyphenation within horizontal lists containing boxes, glue, rules, ligatures, kerns, discretionaries, mathwhatsits, punctuation, etc.; punctuation or ligatures around or within words shouldn't prevent recognition, but TeX intentionally uses simple, fast heuristics to avoid spending time on unusual cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The algorithm aims to be fast and robust; authors can add exceptions if the patterns are insufficient for their context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation-related integer and dimension parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX's hyphenation behavior and frequency can be influenced by parameters such as \hyphenpenalty, \doublehyphendemerits, \pretolerance, \tolerance, \finalhyphendemerits, \lefthyphenmin, \righthyphenmin, and \hyphenchar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These parameters control how eager TeX is to hyphenate, penalties for single/double hyphens, tolerances in breaking paragraphs, and minimum letters before/after hyphenation. The appendix shows examples of setting these to force more hyphenation for demonstration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception vs pattern tradeoff and practical expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain TeX's patterns find ~90% of permissible hyphen points overall, but when word frequency is considered they effectively cover >95% of likely needs; manual intervention (exception additions) is rarely necessary and, when needed, is cheap relative to proofreading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patterns generalize well to new coined or rare words similar to common patterns; use \hyphenation to add high-frequency misses for a specific job.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on exception entries (character and category constraints)
rubrics_metrics.description: In \hyphenation entries a 'letter' is restricted to tokens of category 11 or 12 or control sequences defined by \chardef/\char whose corresponding character has nonzero \lccode; any hyphenation entry must be made of such letters and hyphens (token - of code 12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enforces that exception words are composed of characters TeX can lowercase and match reliably; otherwise they won't behave as expected.
